headline: A photograph of the US Treasury building now leads this page; no finding changed.
summary: Picture only: added a public-domain photograph of the US Treasury Department building (Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons) as the page's picture. Its caption says FinCEN is a Treasury bureau and that this is not FinCEN's own office. No claim, label, source or question changed, and this is not a check of the story.

headline: Some FinCEN systems are still offline; FinCEN has still not said who got in, how, or whether any data was taken.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read the BSA E-Filing alert (s001) at 3:07 PM ET: wording unchanged, some systems still offline, website operational, no restoration time; service stays down (c002). No new FinCEN, Treasury, FBI or CISA statement found naming an attacker or method (q002 open), on whether data was taken (q003 open), or linking or separating it from the reported CIA and ODNI breach (q005 open). CyberScoop, Cybersecurity News and a local ABC affiliate (Nov 25) repeat FinCEN's statements; CyberScoop still says it is unclear whether the two incidents are related. No claim of responsibility in reputable outlets; older Treasury breaches attributed to China have not been linked to this one. Staleness check done: head still true. Not yet eligible for resolved: service is down.

headline: FinCEN gives affected filers until Dec 30 for reports due since Nov 18; some of its systems are still offline.
summary: Added FinCEN Order FIN-2026-R002 of Nov 24 (s004, Tier 1, read on fincen.gov). It extends deadlines for submissions due Nov 18 to Dec 29, 2026 to Dec 30, for institutions that used Secure Data Transfer Mode to file BSA reports as of Nov 18, and for beneficial ownership reports and FinCEN ID updates. c003 rewritten to carry the date and scope; t003 added; who_is_affected and figures updated. Re-read the BSA E-Filing alert (s001) at 1:05 PM ET: unchanged, some systems still offline, website up; service stays down (c002). No FinCEN or Treasury press release about the incident itself; no FBI or CISA statement found. CyberScoop, ABC News and others repeat FinCEN's statements; not new. One outlet (TFTC) says batch filing failures began about Nov 18, citing no source we could open; not added. Outlets say it is unclear whether the incident is linked to the reported intelligence-agency breach (q005 stays open). The Verge, SecurityWeek and Cybernews were not checked: access blocked. Not yet eligible for resolved: service is down.

headline: FinCEN says someone gained unauthorized access to some of its systems; some systems are offline and filing deadlines are being extended.
summary: New incident page. Read FinCEN's service-disruption alert on the BSA E-Filing site (Tier 1), Reuters' report of a FinCEN official's statement (via KFGO) and The Record. Main answer Confirmed on FinCEN's own notice; answer_group hack-stated. Service: down (some systems offline, website up). FBI/CISA role and 'no evidence of database breach' are FinCEN's word, Reported. Attacker and any link to the reported CIA breach: Not established. The Verge first reported it; not opened. Privacy check done: no names, handles, emails or phone numbers.
